# describe: the exact tag when HEAD is tagged, else <tag>-<n>-g<sha>[-dirty].

# self-explanatory.
VERSION="$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0.0-dev)"
VERSION="${VERSION#v}"
echo "$VERSION" > "$BUNDLE_DIR/version.txt"
echo "→ Built fa v$VERSION"

echo "→ Installing to $INSTALL_DIR..."
cp "$BUNDLE_DIR/bin/fah" "$INSTALL_DIR/fa"
chmod +x "$INSTALL_DIR/fa"
# macOS ARM kills unsigned native executables; ad-hoc sign so the copied
# binary is allowed to run from ~/.local/bin.
if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  codesign -s - -f "$INSTALL_DIR/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
cp "$BUNDLE_DIR/version.txt" "$INSTALL_DIR/version.txt"
if [ -d "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib" ]; then
  cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/" 2>/dev/null || true

if ! command -v fa >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "⚠  $INSTALL_DIR is not on your PATH. Add this to your shell rc:"
  echo "   export PATH=\"\$PATH:$INSTALL_DIR\""
else
  INSTALLED_VERSION="$(fa --version)"

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

# gh-1574: [BUG] read tool on .db/.sqlite fails: libsqlite3.dylib not found (installer puts it in bin/lib, binary looks in ../lib)

## Description

## Summary
The builtin `read` tool on a `.db/.sqlite` file fails on fa 1.0.565 (macOS arm64, installed in `~/.local/bin/fa`):

```
Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' ... Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)
```

## Reproduction
`read path=~/.fah/ledger.db` (any SQLite database).

## Cause
The binary resolves `../lib/libsqlite3.dylib` relative to `fa`, i.e. `~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`, but the installer places the bundle libs in `~/.local/bin/lib/` (`install_local.sh` and `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` both copy to `<installDir>/lib`). On this machine the dylib lives at `~/.local/bin/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`; it only worked because of a manual symlink at `~/.local/lib/`.

## Expected (either)
- Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`), or make the binary look in `<installDir>/lib` too; and/or
- Fall back to the system library (`/usr/lib/libsqlite3.dylib` on macOS, `libsqlite3.so.0` on Linux) when the bundled one is missing.
- A missing library must produce a clean "sqlite unavailable" note, as the tool does when no engine is wired, rather than a raw FFI error.

## Tests
Installer layout test (dylib reachable from the binary's lookup path) and an engine-loader test with a missing bundled lib falling back / degrading cleanly.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it

  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via

  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars

  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill

  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install_local.sh — build the Fa CLI from source and install it locally to ~/.local/bin.
#
# Run from the repo root:
#   sh install_local.sh

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
BUNDLE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/fa-local/bundle"
INSTALL_DIR="${INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"

mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

echo "→ Building Fa CLI bundle..."
dart pub get >/dev/null 2>&1 || dart pub get
dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local

# gh-1522: the committed pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder (the git
# tag is the single source of truth) — stamp the build version from git
# describe: the exact tag when HEAD is tagged, else <tag>-<n>-g<sha>[-dirty].
# A plain `dart run` (no install) shows 0.0.0-dev — acceptable and
# self-explanatory.
VERSION="$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0.0-dev)"
VERSION="${VERSION#v}"
echo "$VERSION" > "$BUNDLE_DIR/version.txt"
echo "→ Built fa v$VERSION"

echo "→ Installing to $INSTALL_DIR..."
cp "$BUNDLE_DIR/bin/fah" "$INSTALL_DIR/fa"
chmod +x "$INSTALL_DIR/fa"
# macOS ARM kills unsigned native executables; ad-hoc sign so the copied
# binary is allowed to run from ~/.local/bin.
if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  codesign -s - -f "$INSTALL_DIR/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
cp "$BUNDLE_DIR/version.txt" "$INSTALL_DIR/version.txt"
if [ -d "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib" ]; then
  cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

echo "→ Installed $INSTALL_DIR/fa"

if ! command -v fa >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "⚠  $INSTALL_DIR is not on your PATH. Add this to your shell rc:"
  echo "   export PATH=\"\$PATH:$INSTALL_DIR\""
else
  INSTALLED_VERSION="$(fa --version)"
  echo "✔  $INSTALLED_VERSION is on PATH"
fi

Dart's `dart build cli` bundle layout: the bundle is `fa-local/bin/fah` plus `fa-local/lib/` — the native assets layout of Dart puts libs in `<bundle>/lib`, and the binary looks in `<binary_dir>/../lib` (standard bundle relative layout). When the installer copies the binary to `~/.local/bin/fa` and the libs to `~/.local/bin/lib`, the relative path from the binary to the lib becomes `~/.local/lib` instead of `~/.local/bin/lib`.

2. Or there's explicit code in `bin/self_manage.dart` (`_copyBundleLibs`) that does the copy.

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

{"path":"input/gh-1574/ticket.json"}
{"path":"lib/src/tools/sqlite"}

{
  "key": "gh-1574",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "[BUG] read tool on .db/.sqlite fails: libsqlite3.dylib not found (installer puts it in bin/lib, binary looks in ../lib)",
    "description": "## Summary
The builtin `read` tool on a `.db/.sqlite` file fails on fa 1.0.565 (macOS arm64, installed in `~/.local/bin/fa`):

```
Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' ... Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)
```

## Reproduction
`read path=~/.fah/ledger.db` (any SQLite database).

## Cause
The binary resolves `../lib/libsqlite3.dylib` relative to `fa`, i.e. `~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`, but the installer places the bundle libs in `~/.local/bin/lib/` (`install_local.sh` and `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` both copy to `<installDir>/lib`). On this machine the dylib lives at `~/.local/bin/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`; it only worked because of a manual symlink at `~/.local/lib/`.

## Expected (either)
- Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`), or make the binary look in `<installDir>/lib` too; and/or
- Fall back to the system library (`/usr/lib/libsqlite3.dylib` on macOS, `libsqlite3.so.0` on Linux) when the bundled one is missing.
- A missing library must produce a clean "sqlite unavailable" note, as the tool does when no engine is wired, rather than a raw FFI error.

## Tests
Installer layout test (dylib reachable from the binary's lookup path) and an engine-loader test with a missing bundled lib falling back / degrading cleanly."
  }
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install_local.sh — build the Fa CLI from source and install it locally to ~/.local/bin.
#
# Run from the repo root:
#   sh install_local.sh

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
BUNDLE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/fa-local/bundle"
INSTALL_DIR="${INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"

mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

echo "→ Building Fa CLI bundle..."
dart pub get >/dev/null 2>&1 || dart pub get
dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local

# gh-1522: the committed pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder (the git
# tag is the single source of truth) — stamp the build version from git
# describe: the exact tag when HEAD is tagged, else <tag>-<n>-g<sha>[-dirty].
# A plain `dart run` (no install) shows 0.0.0-dev — acceptable and
# self-explanatory.
VERSION="$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0.0-dev)"
VERSION="${VERSION#v}"
echo "$VERSION" > "$BUNDLE_DIR/version.txt"
echo "→ Built fa v$VERSION"

echo "→ Installing to $INSTALL_DIR..."
cp "$BUNDLE_DIR/bin/fah" "$INSTALL_DIR/fa"
chmod +x "$INSTALL_DIR/fa"
# macOS ARM kills unsigned native executables; ad-hoc sign so the copied
# binary is allowed to run from ~/.local/bin.
if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  codesign -s - -f "$INSTALL_DIR/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
cp "$BUNDLE_DIR/version.txt" "$INSTALL_DIR/version.txt"
if [ -d "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib" ]; then
  cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

echo "→ Installed $INSTALL_DIR/fa"

if ! command -v fa >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "⚠  $INSTALL_DIR is not on your PATH. Add this to your shell rc:"
  echo "   export PATH=\"\$PATH:$INSTALL_DIR\""
else
  INSTALLED_VERSION="$(fa --version)"
  echo "✔  $INSTALLED_VERSION is on PATH"
fi

When the installer copies the binary to `~/.local/bin/fa` and the libs to `~/.local/bin/lib`, the relative path from the binary to the lib becomes `~/.local/lib` instead of `~/.local/bin/lib`.

2. Or there's explicit code in `bin/self_manage.dart` (`_copyBundleLibs`) that does the copy.

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install_local.sh — build the Fa CLI from source and install it locally to ~/.local/bin.
#
# Run from the repo root:
#   sh install_local.sh

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
BUNDLE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/fa-local/bundle"
INSTALL_DIR="${INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"

mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

echo "→ Building Fa CLI bundle..."
dart pub get >/dev/null 2>&1 || dart pub get
dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local

# gh-1522: the committed pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder (the git
# tag is the single source of truth) — stamp the build version from git
# describe: the exact tag when HEAD is tagged, else <tag>-<n>-g<sha>[-dirty].
# A plain `dart run` (no install) shows 0.0.0-dev — acceptable and
# self-explanatory.
VERSION="$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0.0-dev)"
VERSION="${VERSION#v}"
echo "$VERSION" > "$BUNDLE_DIR/version.txt"
echo "→ Built fa v$VERSION"

echo "→ Installing to $INSTALL_DIR..."
cp "$BUNDLE_DIR/bin/fah" "$INSTALL_DIR/fa"
chmod +x "$INSTALL_DIR/fa"
# macOS ARM kills unsigned native executables; ad-hoc sign so the copied
# binary is allowed to run from ~/.local/bin.
if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  codesign -s - -f "$INSTALL_DIR/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
cp "$BUNDLE_DIR/version.txt" "$INSTALL_DIR/version.txt"
if [ -d "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib" ]; then
  cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

echo "→ Installed $INSTALL_DIR/fa"

if ! command -v fa >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "⚠  $INSTALL_DIR is not on your PATH. Add this to your shell rc:"
  echo "   export PATH=\"\$PATH:$INSTALL_DIR\""
else
  INSTALLED_VERSION="$(fa --version)"

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install_local.sh — build the Fa CLI from source and install it locally to ~/.local/bin.
#
# Run from the repo root:
#   sh install_local.sh

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
BUNDLE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/fa-local/bundle"
INSTALL_DIR="${INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"

mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

echo "→ Building Fa CLI bundle..."
dart pub get >/dev/null 2>&1 || dart pub get
dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local

# gh-1522: the committed pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder (the git
# tag is the single source of truth) — stamp the build version from git
# describe: the exact tag when HEAD is tagged, else <tag>-<n>-g<sha>[-dirty].
# A plain `dart run` (no install) shows 0.0.0-dev — acceptable and
# self-explanatory.
VERSION="$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0.0-dev)"
VERSION="${VERSION#v}"
echo "$VERSION" > "$BUNDLE_DIR/version.txt"
echo "→ Built fa v$VERSION"

echo "→ Installing to $INSTALL_DIR..."
cp "$BUNDLE_DIR/bin/fah" "$INSTALL_DIR/fa"
chmod +x "$INSTALL_DIR/fa"
# macOS ARM kills unsigned native executables; ad-hoc sign so the copied
# binary is allowed to run from ~/.local/bin.
if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  codesign -s - -f "$INSTALL_DIR/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
cp "$BUNDLE_DIR/version.txt" "$INSTALL_DIR/version.txt"
if [ -d "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib" ]; then
  cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

echo "→ Installed $INSTALL_DIR/fa"

if ! command -v fa >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "⚠  $INSTALL_DIR is not on your PATH. Add this to your shell rc:"
  echo "   export PATH=\"\$PATH:$INSTALL_DIR\""
else
  INSTALLED_VERSION="$(fa --version)"
  echo "✔  $INSTALLED_VERSION is on PATH"

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install_local.sh — build the Fa CLI from source and install it locally to ~/.local/bin.
#
# Run from the repo root:
#   sh install_local.sh

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
BUNDLE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/fa-local/bundle"
INSTALL_DIR="${INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"

mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

echo "→ Building Fa CLI bundle..."
dart pub get >/dev/null 2>&1 || dart pub get
dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local

# gh-1522: the committed pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder (the git
# tag is the single source of truth) — stamp the build version from git
# describe: the exact tag when HEAD is tagged, else <tag>-<n>-g<sha>[-dirty].
# A plain `dart run` (no install) shows 0.0.0-dev — acceptable and
# self-explanatory.
VERSION="$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0.0-dev)"
VERSION="${VERSION#v}"
echo "$VERSION" > "$BUNDLE_DIR/version.txt"
echo "→ Built fa v$VERSION"

echo "→ Installing to $INSTALL_DIR..."
cp "$BUNDLE_DIR/bin/fah" "$INSTALL_DIR/fa"
chmod +x "$INSTALL_DIR/fa"
# macOS ARM kills unsigned native executables; ad-hoc sign so the copied
# binary is allowed to run from ~/.local/bin.
if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  codesign -s - -f "$INSTALL_DIR/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
cp "$BUNDLE_DIR/version.txt" "$INSTALL_DIR/version.txt"
if [ -d "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib" ]; then
  cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

echo "→ Installed $INSTALL_DIR/fa"

if ! command -v fa >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "⚠  $INSTALL_DIR is not on your PATH. Add this to your shell rc:"
  echo "   export PATH=\"\$PATH:$INSTALL_DIR\""
else
  INSTALLED_VERSION="$(fa --version)"
  echo "✔  $INSTALLED_VERSION is on PATH"
fi

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
BUNDLE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/fa-local/bundle"
INSTALL_DIR="${INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"

mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

echo "→ Building Fa CLI bundle..."
dart pub get >/dev/null 2>&1 || dart pub get
dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local

# gh-1522: the committed pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder (the git
# tag is the single source of truth) — stamp the build version from git
# describe: the exact tag when HEAD is tagged, else <tag>-<n>-g<sha>[-dirty].
# A plain `dart run` (no install) shows 0.0.0-dev — acceptable and
# self-explanatory.
VERSION="$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0.0-dev)"
VERSION="${VERSION#v}"
echo "$VERSION" > "$BUNDLE_DIR/version.txt"
echo "→ Built fa v$VERSION"

echo "→ Installing to $INSTALL_DIR..."
cp "$BUNDLE_DIR/bin/fah" "$INSTALL_DIR/fa"
chmod +x "$INSTALL_DIR/fa"
# macOS ARM kills unsigned native executables; ad-hoc sign so the copied
# binary is allowed to run from ~/.local/bin.
if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  codesign -s - -f "$INSTALL_DIR/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
cp "$BUNDLE_DIR/version.txt" "$INSTALL_DIR/version.txt"
if [ -d "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib" ]; then
  cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

echo "→ Installed $INSTALL_DIR/fa"

if ! command -v fa >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "⚠  $INSTALL_DIR is not on your PATH. Add this to your shell rc:"
  echo "   export PATH=\"\$PATH:$INSTALL_DIR\""
else
  INSTALLED_VERSION="$(fa --version)"
  echo "✔  $INSTALLED_VERSION is on PATH"
fi

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

[ "$trust_pem" = "${FA_SIGNING_PEM:-}" ] || rm -f "$trust_pem"

# dart build cli produces a bundle/ dir: bundle/bin/fa + bundle/lib/*.dylib
# Extract into a TEMP dir — nothing touches the install directory until the
# artifact above has passed the provenance gate.
tmp_extract="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t fa-extract)"
if ! tar -xzf "$tmp_archive" -C "$tmp_extract" 2>/dev/null; then
  err "E_ARCHIVE_CORRUPT: downloaded archive is corrupt or empty. Nothing was installed."
  rm -rf "$tmp_extract" "$tmp_archive"
  exit 1
fi
rm -f "$tmp_archive"

# macOS code-signature identity check (SEC-07 contract 3): verified BEFORE
# the binary lands in the install directory. Release CLI binaries are
# ad-hoc signed today — their provenance is the signed-checksum gate above;
# once releases carry a real Developer ID identity, set (or bake in)
# FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER to enforce the publisher identity and abort otherwise.
if [ "$os" = "macos" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -n "${FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER:-}" ]; then
  if ! codesign --verify --strict "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    err "E_CODESIGN_INVALID: the binary's code signature is invalid for release $FA_VERSION. Nothing was installed."
    rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
    exit 1
  fi
  authority="$(codesign -dv "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^Authority=//p' | head -1)"
  case "$authority" in
    # Anchored (gh-814 r2): the expected identity must PREFIX the signing
    # authority — a substring match would accept lookalike CN fragments.
    "$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER"*)
      ok "Code signature identity verified: $authority"
      ;;
    "")
      err "E_SIGNER_MISSING: expected signer '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER' but the binary carries no signature identity. Nothing was installed."
      rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
      exit 1
      ;;
    *)
      err "E_SIGNER_MISMATCH: binary signed by '$authority', expected '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER'. Nothing was installed."
      rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
fi

mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"
rm -f "$target"  # break any pre-existing symlink so cp writes the real file
cp "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" "$target"
chmod +x "$target"
# Copy version.txt so the binary can report its version.
if [ -f "$tmp_extract/bundle/version.txt" ]; then
  cp "$tmp_extract/bundle/version.txt" "$install_dir/version.txt"
fi
if [ -d "$tmp_extract/bundle/lib" ]; then
  cp -r "$tmp_extract/bundle/lib/"* "$install_dir/lib/" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

rm -f "$tmp_archive"

# macOS code-signature identity check (SEC-07 contract 3): verified BEFORE
# the binary lands in the install directory. Release CLI binaries are
# ad-hoc signed today — their provenance is the signed-checksum gate above;
# once releases carry a real Developer ID identity, set (or bake in)
# FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER to enforce the publisher identity and abort otherwise.
if [ "$os" = "macos" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -n "${FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER:-}" ]; then
  if ! codesign --verify --strict "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    err "E_CODESIGN_INVALID: the binary's code signature is invalid for release $FA_VERSION. Nothing was installed."
    rm -rf "$tmp_extract"

  case "$authority" in
    # Anchored (gh-814 r2): the expected identity must PREFIX the signing
    # authority — a substring match would accept lookalike CN fragments.
    "$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER"*)
      ok "Code signature identity verified: $authority"
      ;;
    "")
      err "E_SIGNER_MISSING: expected signer '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER' but the binary carries no signature identity. Nothing was installed."

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

blocks.text:
# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

Full picture now. Installers that place the binary + libs:

1. **`site/install.sh`** (the curl installer, POSIX): `install_dir="${FA_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"`, exe → `$install_dir/fa`, libs → `$install_dir/lib/`. **BROKEN** — binary looks in `$install_dir/../lib`.
   Also line 369: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "$install_dir/lib"`.

2. **`install_local.sh`** (build-from-source): `INSTALL_DIR="${INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"`, exe → `$INSTALL_DIR/fa`, libs → `$INSTALL_DIR/lib/`. **BROKEN** same way.

3. **`bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs`**: exe → `<installDir>/fa`, libs → `<installDir>/lib/`. **BROKEN** same way.

4. **`site/install.ps1`** (Windows): `$binDir = Join-Path $installDir "bin"`, exe → `$binDir\fa.exe`, libs → `$installDir\lib`. Lookup `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `$installDir\lib` — **CORRECT** already! That's why the uninstall deletes the grandparent ("the release layout is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Fa\bin\fa.exe`"). So Windows is fine; the POSIX layout (exe directly in the install dir) is the broken one.

So the root cause: on POSIX installs, the binary sits DIRECTLY in the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) while the native-assets runtime resolves the bundled dylib as `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` = `~/.local/lib/<name>` — but every POSIX installer copies the libs to `<exe_dir>/lib` = `~/.local/bin/lib`.

Two coherent fix directions:

**A. Change the POSIX installers to install the exe under a `bin/` subdir?** — No, that changes PATH semantics (`~/.local/bin` must stay on PATH; putting it in a nested `bin/` breaks the `~/.local/bin/fa` contract). Bad.

**B. Change the POSIX installers to put libs in `<install_dir>/../lib`** — matches the binary's native-assets lookup: `~/.local/bin/fa` + `../lib` = `~/.local/lib`. This is exactly the ticket's first Expected option ("Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`)").

Then:
- **Clean degradation**: the engine maps the native-assets load failure to a clean StateError (the ticket's third expectation). "Fall back to the system library" is impossible at Dart level with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (no override API; the VM resolver doesn't fall back) — so the honest implementation is the clean "sqlite unavailable" note telling the user to reinstall/update. I'll document that.

Wait — actually, let me double-check whether a system fallback is truly impossible. Hmm, one more idea: `@ffi.DefaultAsset` on the generated bindings — we can't change package code. Could we set an environment variable like `DART_NATIVE_ASSETS`? No such override. There is `DynamicLibrary.open('libsqlite3.dylib')` fallback INSIDE the VM resolver? The probe error shows only the mapped relative path attempt — single shot. Confirmed impossible without forking the package. (For the ticket's "either/or" wording, the installer fix + clean note satisfies it; the system-fallback bullet was one of several alternatives — "and/or".)

Hmm wait, actually, let me reconsider — is there really no way to preload the library? With native assets, symbols are resolved against the mapped library — `DynamicLibrary.open('/usr/libsqlite3.dylib')` on our own wouldn't help the `@ffi.Native` bindings (they resolve via the asset mapping, not a handle we hold). Correct, impossible.

So final fix plan:

**1. `site/install.sh`** — copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` instead of `$install_dir/lib`:

   - line 369: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "$install_dir/lib"` → new target.
   Also the source-run fallback instructions at line 213-214: `cp build/out/bundle/bin/fah ~/.local/bin/fa` — add `cp -r build/out/bundle/lib ~/.local/lib/`? That's an advisory string; update it to keep the layout contract visible. Let me read the whole file section first.

**2. `install_local.sh`** — same: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"` + `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"` → `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.

**3. `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs`** — copy to `<installDir>/../lib`. BUT: Windows! On Windows, `installDir` = `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Fa\bin` (exe at `$installDir\fa.exe`)? Wait no — check: `_binaryUpdate`: `target = install.executable`; `installDir = File(target).parent`. On Windows the target is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Fa\bin\fa.exe` so installDir = `...\Fa\bin`, and the native-assets lookup is `...\Fa\lib` — the CURRENT code copies to `...\Fa\bin\lib` which is WRONG on Windows too?! But install.ps1 copies to `$installDir\lib` = `...\Fa\lib` which is RIGHT. So `fa update` on Windows would ALSO break the lookup (copies to the wrong place). Changing `_copyBundleLibs` to `<installDir>/../lib` fixes Windows `fa update` as well and unifies with install.ps1.

# Extract into a TEMP dir — nothing touches the install directory until the

tmp_extract="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t fa-extract)"
if ! tar -xzf "$tmp_archive" -C "$tmp_extract" 2>/dev/null; then
  err "E_ARCHIVE_CORRUPT: downloaded archive is corrupt or empty. Nothing was installed."
  rm -rf "$tmp_extract" "$tmp_archive"
  exit 1
fi
rm -f "$tmp_archive"

# macOS code-signature identity check (SEC-07 contract 3): verified BEFORE
# the binary lands in the install directory. Release CLI binaries are
# ad-hoc signed today — their provenance is the signed-checksum gate above;
# once releases carry a real Developer ID identity, set (or bake in)
# FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER to enforce the publisher identity and abort otherwise.
if [ "$os" = "macos" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -n "${FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER:-}" ]; then
  if ! codesign --verify --strict "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    err "E_CODESIGN_INVALID: the binary's code signature is invalid for release $FA_VERSION. Nothing was installed."
    rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
    exit 1
  fi
  authority="$(codesign -dv "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^Authority=//p' | head -1)"
  case "$authority" in
    # Anchored (gh-814 r2): the expected identity must PREFIX the signing
    # authority — a substring match would accept lookalike CN fragments.
    "$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER"*)
      ok "Code signature identity verified: $authority"
      ;;
    "")
      err "E_SIGNER_MISSING: expected signer '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER' but the binary carries no signature identity. Nothing was installed."
      rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
      exit 1
      ;;
    *)
      err "E_SIGNER_MISMATCH: binary signed by '$authority', expected '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER'. Nothing was installed."
      rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
fi

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).
"}

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```
