**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

1. **`site/install.sh`** (the curl installer, POSIX): `install_dir="${FA_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"`, exe → `$install_dir/fa`, libs → `$install_dir/lib/`. **BROKEN** — binary looks in `$install_dir/../lib`.

2. **`install_local.sh`** (build-from-source): `INSTALL_DIR="${INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"`, exe → `$INSTALL_DIR/fa`, libs → `$INSTALL_DIR/lib/`. **BROKEN** same way.

3. **`bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs`**: exe → `<installDir>/fa`, libs → `<installDir>/lib/`. **BROKEN** same way.

4. **`site/install.ps1`** (Windows): `$binDir = Join-Path $installDir "bin"`, exe → `$binDir\fa.exe`, libs → `$installDir\lib`. Lookup `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `$installDir\lib` — **CORRECT** already! That's why the uninstall deletes the grandparent ("the release layout is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Fa\bin\fa.exe`"). So Windows is fine; the POSIX layout (exe directly in the install dir) is the broken one.

So the root cause: on POSIX installs, the binary sits DIRECTLY in the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) while the native-assets runtime resolves the bundled dylib as `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` = `~/.local/lib/<name>` — but every POSIX installer copies the libs to `<exe_dir>/lib` = `~/.local/bin/lib`.

Two coherent fix directions:

**A. Change the POSIX installers to install the exe under a `bin/` subdir?** — No, that changes PATH semantics (`~/.local/bin` must stay on PATH; putting it in a nested `bin/` breaks the `~/.local/bin/fa` contract). Bad.

**B. Change the POSIX installers to put libs in `<install_dir>/../lib`** — matches the binary's native-assets lookup: `~/.local/bin/fa` + `../lib` = `~/.local/lib`. This is exactly the ticket's first Expected option ("Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`)").

Then:
- **Clean degradation**: the engine maps the native-assets load failure to a clean StateError (the ticket's third expectation). {"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

1. **`site/install.sh`** (the curl installer, POSIX): `install_dir="${FA_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"`, exe → `$install_dir/fa`, libs → `$install_dir/lib/`. **BROKEN** — binary looks in `$install_dir/../lib`.

2. **`install_local.sh`** (build-from-source): `INSTALL_DIR="${INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"`, exe → `$INSTALL_DIR/fa`, libs → `$INSTALL_DIR/lib/`. **BROKEN** same way.

3. **`bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs`**: exe → `<installDir>/fa`, libs → `<installDir>/lib/`. **BROKEN** same way.

That's why the uninstall deletes the grandparent ("the release layout is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Fa\bin\fa.exe`"). So Windows is fine; the POSIX layout (exe directly in the install dir) is the broken one.

So the root cause: on POSIX installs, the binary sits DIRECTLY in the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) while the native-assets runtime resolves the bundled dylib as `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` = `~/.local/lib/<name>` — but every POSIX installer copies the libs to `<exe_dir>/lib` = `~/.local/bin/lib`.

# Extract into a TEMP dir — nothing touches the install directory until the
# artifact above has passed the provenance gate.
tmp_extract="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t fa-extract)"
if ! tar -xzf "$tmp_archive" -C "$tmp_extract" 2>/dev/null; then
  err "E_ARCHIVE_CORRUPT: downloaded archive is corrupt or empty. Nothing was installed."
  rm -rf "$tmp_extract" "$tmp_archive"
  exit 1
fi
rm -f "$tmp_archive"

# macOS code-signature identity check (SEC-07 contract 3): verified BEFORE
# the binary lands in the install directory. Release CLI binaries are
# ad-hoc signed today — their provenance is the signed-checksum gate above;
# once releases carry a real Developer ID identity, set (or bake in)
# FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER to enforce the publisher identity and abort otherwise.
if [ "$os" = "macos" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -n "${FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER:-}" ]; then
  if ! codesign --verify --strict "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    err "E_CODESIGN_INVALID: the binary's code signature is invalid for release $FA_VERSION. Nothing was installed."
    rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
    exit 1
  fi
  authority="$(codesign -dv "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^Authority=//p' | head -1)"
  case "$authority" in
    # Anchored (gh-814 r2): the expected identity must PREFIX the signing
    # authority — a substring match would accept lookalike CN fragments.
    "$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER"*)
      ok "Code signature identity verified: $authority"
      ;;
    "")
      err "E_SIGNER_MISSING: expected signer '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER' but the binary carries no signature identity. Nothing was installed."
      rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
      exit 1
      ;;
    *)
      err "E_SIGNER_MISMATCH: binary signed by '$authority', expected '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER'. Nothing was installed."
      rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
fi

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

# macOS code-signature identity check (SEC-07 contract 3): verified BEFORE
# the binary lands in the install directory. Release CLI binaries are
# ad-hoc signed today — their provenance is the signed-checksum gate above;
# once releases carry a real Developer ID identity, set (or bake in)
# FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER to enforce the publisher identity and abort otherwise.
if [ "$os" = "macos" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -n "${FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER:-}" ]; then
  if ! codesign --verify --strict "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    err "E_CODESIGN_INVALID: the binary's code signature is invalid for release $FA_VERSION. Nothing was installed."
    rm -rf "$tmp_extract"

  authority="$(codesign -dv "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^Authority=//p' | head -1)"
  case "$authority" in
    # Anchored (gh-814 r2): the expected identity must PREFIX the signing
    # authority — a substring match would accept lookalike CN fragments.
    "$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER"*)
      ok "Code signature identity verified: $authority"
      ;;
    "")
      err "E_SIGNER_MISSING: expected signer '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER' but the binary carries no signature identity. Nothing was installed."

      err "E_SIGNER_MISMATCH: binary signed by '$authority', expected '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER'. Nothing was installed."

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

# SQLite for Dart

Provides Dart bindings to [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html), both on native platforms
and the web.

## Installation

Because this library uses [hooks](https://dart.dev/tools/hooks), it bundles SQLite with
your application and doesn't require any external dependencies or build configuration.
To use it, depend on it:

```shell
dart pub add sqlite3
```

To use this library on the web, additional setup is necessary:

- You need a copy of SQLite as a WebAssembly module, available from the
  [GitHub releases](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases) of this package.
  Note that, for this package, __sqlite3 has to be compiled in a special way__.
  Existing WebAssembly files from e.g. sql.js will not work with `package:sqlite3/wasm.dart`.
  You can also see [this directory](https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/tree/main/sqlite3_wasm_build)
  for the build files to compile this yourself.
- Because websites can't access the host's file system, this also needs a
  virtual file system implementation. This package provides `InMemoryFileSystem`,
  `IndexedDbFileSystem` and OPFS-based file system implementations.

> [!TIP]
> This package provides direct and synchronous access to SQLite. For most apps, running SQLite in a background
> isolate or web worker is a much better option, and there are packages to help you with that:
> [`sqlite_async`](https://pub.dev/packages/sqlite_async) and sqflite (through [sqflite_common_ffi](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi) and [sqflite_common_ffi_web](https://pub.dev/packages/sqflite_common_ffi_web))
> provide common interfaces and platform-specific asynchronous implementations.
>
> Additionally, projects like [drift](https://drift.simonbinder.eu), [raindrop](https://pub.dev/packages/raindrop) and [typed_sql](https://pub.dev/packages/typed_sql)
> provide type-safety for SQL queries.

## Opening databases

While using SQLite on native platforms is straightforward, using it on the web requires additional setup to
load the WebAssembly module.

### Native

On native platforms, use the `sqlite3` constant to open databases:

```dart
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';

void main() {
  final db = sqlite3.open('test.db');
  db
    ..execute(
      'CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT) STRICT',
    )
    ..execute('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', ['SQLite user']);

  print(db.select('SELECT * FROM users'));
}
```

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).
"}

Reproduced the exact mechanism:

- The AOT binary resolves the bundled asset as **`../libsqlite3.so` relative to the executable** — i.e. `<exe_dir>/../lib/`.
- Installer layout (exe at `<installDir>/fa`, lib at `<installDir>/libsqlite3.so`) → lookup `<installDir>/../libsqlite3.so` → **not found**. On macOS the error text names `/Users/<user>/.local/libsqlite3.dylib`… hmm wait the ticket error says `/Users/<user>/.local/libsqlite3.dylib`. On macOS it may be `../libsqlite3.dylib` without `lib/`? Let me check the macOS variant: the error here on Linux says `'../libsqlite3.so' relative to '/tmp/na_probe/flat/fa': Failed to load dynamic library '/tmp/na_probe/libsqlite3.so'`.

So the lookup path = `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>`. On the user's machine: exe `~/.local/bin/fa` → `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` — and the ticket error says `Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`. Let me re-read the ticket: "Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)". YES — it says `.local/libsqlite3.dylib`. And "On this machine the dylib lives at `~/.local/bin/libsqlite3.dylib`; it only worked because of a manual symlink at `~/.local/lib/`." — consistent! (The title "installer puts it in bin/lib" also consistent.)

- Dart native-assets runtime lookup: `<exe_dir>/../lib/` (relative to the installed binary).
- Installer (`install_local.sh` + `bin/self_manage.dart _copyBundleLibs`): `<installDir>/lib/` where `<installDir>` = the exe's own directory (`~/.local/bin/lib/`).
- Mismatch: `~/.local/bin/../lib` = `~/.local/lib` vs `~/.local/bin/lib`.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).
"}

Reproduced the exact mechanism:

- The AOT binary resolves the bundled asset as **`../libsqlite3.so` relative to the executable** — i.e. `<exe_dir>/../lib/`.
- Installer layout (exe at `<installDir>/fa`, lib at `<installDir>/libsqlite3.so`) → lookup `<installDir>/../libsqlite3.so` → **not found**. On macOS the error text names `/Users/<user>/.local/libsqlite3.dylib`… hmm wait the ticket error says `/Users/<user>/.local/libsqlite3.dylib`. On macOS it may be `../libsqlite3.dylib` without `lib/`? Let me check the macOS variant: the error here on Linux says `'../libsqlite3.so' relative to '/tmp/na_probe/flat/fa': Failed to load dynamic library '/tmp/na_probe/libsqlite3.so'`.

So the lookup path = `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>`. On the user's machine: exe `~/.local/bin/fa` → `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` — and the ticket error says `Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`. Let me re-read the ticket: "Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)". YES — it says `.local/libsqlite3.dylib`. And "On this machine the dylib lives at `~/.local/bin/libsqlite3.dylib`; it only worked because of a manual symlink at `~/.local/lib/`." — consistent! (The title "installer puts it in bin/lib" also consistent.)

So root cause confirmed precisely:
- Dart native-assets runtime lookup: `<exe_dir>/../lib/` (relative to the installed binary).
- Installer (`install_local.sh` + `bin/self_manage.dart _copyBundleLibs`): `<installDir>/lib/` where `<installDir>` = the exe's own directory (`~/.local/bin/lib/`).
- Mismatch: `~/.local/bin/../lib` = `~/.local/lib` vs `~/.local/bin/lib`.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).
"}

Full picture now. Installers that place the binary + libs:

1. **`site/install.sh`** (the curl installer, POSIX): `install_dir="${FA_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"`, exe → `$install_dir/fa`, libs → `$install_dir/lib/`. **BROKEN** — binary looks in `$install_dir/../lib`.
   Also line 369: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "$install_dir/lib"`.

2. **`install_local.sh`** (build-from-source): `INSTALL_DIR="${INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"`, exe → `$INSTALL_DIR/fa`, libs → `$INSTALL_DIR/lib/`. **BROKEN** same way.

3. **`bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs`**: exe → `<installDir>/fa`, libs → `<installDir>/lib/`. **BROKEN** same way.

4. **`site/install.ps1`** (Windows): `$binDir = Join-Path $installDir "bin"`, exe → `$binDir\fa.exe`, libs → `$installDir\lib`. Lookup `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `$installDir\lib` — **CORRECT** already! That's why the uninstall deletes the grandparent ("the release layout is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Fa\bin\fa.exe`"). So Windows is fine; the POSIX layout (exe directly in the install dir) is the broken one.

So the root cause: on POSIX installs, the binary sits DIRECTLY in the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) while the native-assets runtime resolves the bundled dylib as `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` = `~/.local/lib/<name>` — but every POSIX installer copies the libs to `<exe_dir>/lib` = `~/.local/bin/lib`.

Two coherent fix directions:

**A. Change the POSIX installers to install the exe under a `bin/` subdir?** — No, that changes PATH semantics (`~/.local/bin` must stay on PATH; putting it in a nested `bin/` breaks the `~/.local/bin/fa` contract). Bad.

**B. Change the POSIX installers to put libs in `<install_dir>/../lib`** — matches the binary's native-assets lookup: `~/.local/bin/fa` + `../lib` = `~/.local/lib`. This is exactly the ticket's first Expected option ("Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`)").

Then:
- **Clean degradation**: the engine maps the native-assets load failure to a clean StateError (the ticket's third expectation). "Fall back to the system library" is impossible at Dart level with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (no override API; the VM resolver doesn't fall back) — so the honest implementation is the clean "sqlite unavailable" note telling the user to reinstall/update. I'll document that.

Could we set an environment variable like `DART_NATIVE_ASSETS`? No such override. There is `DynamicLibrary.open('libsqlite3.dylib')` fallback INSIDE the VM resolver? The probe error shows only the mapped relative path attempt — single shot. Confirmed impossible without forking the package. # dart build cli produces a bundle/ dir: bundle/bin/fa + bundle/lib/*.dylib
# Extract into a TEMP dir — nothing touches the install directory until the
# artifact above has passed the provenance gate.
tmp_extract="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t fa-extract)"
if ! tar -xzf "$tmp_archive" -C "$tmp_extract" 2>/dev/null; then
  err "E_ARCHIVE_CORRUPT: downloaded archive is corrupt or empty. Nothing was installed."
  rm -rf "$tmp_extract" "$tmp_archive"
  exit 1
fi
rm -f "$tmp_archive"

# macOS code-signature identity check (SEC-07 contract 3): verified BEFORE
# the binary lands in the install directory. Release CLI binaries are
# ad-hoc signed today — their provenance is the signed-checksum gate above;
# once releases carry a real Developer ID identity, set (or bake in)
# FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER to enforce the publisher identity and abort otherwise.
if [ "$os" = "macos" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -n "${FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER:-}" ]; then
  if ! codesign --verify --strict "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    err "E_CODESIGN_INVALID: the binary's code signature is invalid for release $FA_VERSION. Nothing was installed."
    rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
    exit 1
  fi
  authority="$(codesign -dv "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^Authority=//p' | head -1)"
  case "$authority" in
    # Anchored (gh-814 r2): the expected identity must PREFIX the signing
    # authority — a substring match would accept lookalike CN fragments.
    "$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER"*)
      ok "Code signature identity verified: $authority"
      ;;
    "")
      err "E_SIGNER_MISSING: expected signer '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER' but the binary carries no signature identity. Nothing was installed."
      rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
      exit 1
      ;;
    *)
      err "E_SIGNER_MISMATCH: binary signed by '$authority', expected '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER'. Nothing was installed."
      rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
fi

mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"
rm -f "$target"  # break any pre-existing symlink so cp writes the real file
cp "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" "$target"
chmod +x "$target"
# Copy version.txt so the binary can report its version.
if [ -f "$tmp_extract/bundle/version.txt" ]; then
  cp "$tmp_extract/bundle/version.txt" "$install_dir/version.txt"
fi
if [ -d "$tmp_extract/bundle/lib" ]; then
  cp -r "$tmp_extract/bundle/lib/"* "$install_dir/lib/" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
rm -rf "$tmp_extract"

ok "Installed $target"

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

1. **`site/install.sh`** (the curl installer, POSIX): `install_dir="${FA_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"`, exe → `$install_dir/fa`, libs → `$install_dir/lib/`. **BROKEN** — binary looks in `$install_dir/../lib`.

2. **`install_local.sh`** (build-from-source): `INSTALL_DIR="${INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"`, exe → `$INSTALL_DIR/fa`, libs → `$INSTALL_DIR/lib/`. **BROKEN** same way.

3. **`bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs`**: exe → `<installDir>/fa`, libs → `<installDir>/lib/`. **BROKEN** same way.

That's why the uninstall deletes the grandparent ("the release layout is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Fa\bin\fa.exe`"). So Windows is fine; the POSIX layout (exe directly in the install dir) is the broken one.

So the root cause: on POSIX installs, the binary sits DIRECTLY in the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) while the native-assets runtime resolves the bundled dylib as `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` = `~/.local/lib/<name>` — but every POSIX installer copies the libs to `<exe_dir>/lib` = `~/.local/bin/lib`.

# Extract into a TEMP dir — nothing touches the install directory until the

tmp_extract="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t fa-extract)"
if ! tar -xzf "$tmp_archive" -C "$tmp_extract" 2>/dev/null; then
  err "E_ARCHIVE_CORRUPT: downloaded archive is corrupt or empty. Nothing was installed."
  rm -rf "$tmp_extract" "$tmp_archive"
  exit 1
fi
rm -f "$tmp_archive"

# macOS code-signature identity check (SEC-07 contract 3): verified BEFORE
# the binary lands in the install directory. Release CLI binaries are
# ad-hoc signed today — their provenance is the signed-checksum gate above;
# once releases carry a real Developer ID identity, set (or bake in)
# FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER to enforce the publisher identity and abort otherwise.
if [ "$os" = "macos" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -n "${FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER:-}" ]; then
  if ! codesign --verify --strict "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    err "E_CODESIGN_INVALID: the binary's code signature is invalid for release $FA_VERSION. Nothing was installed."
    rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
    exit 1
  fi
  authority="$(codesign -dv "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^Authority=//p' | head -1)"
  case "$authority" in
    # Anchored (gh-814 r2): the expected identity must PREFIX the signing
    # authority — a substring match would accept lookalike CN fragments.
    "$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER"*)
      ok "Code signature identity verified: $authority"
      ;;
    "")
      err "E_SIGNER_MISSING: expected signer '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER' but the binary carries no signature identity. Nothing was installed."
      rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
      exit 1
      ;;
    *)
      err "E_SIGNER_MISMATCH: binary signed by '$authority', expected '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER'. Nothing was installed."
      rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
      exit 1

fi

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).
