{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

1. **`site/install.sh`** (the curl installer, POSIX): `install_dir="${FA_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"`, exe → `$install_dir/fa`, libs → `$install_dir/lib/`. **BROKEN** — binary looks in `$install_dir/../lib`.

2. **`install_local.sh`** (build-from-source): `INSTALL_DIR="${INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"`, exe → `$INSTALL_DIR/fa`, libs → `$INSTALL_DIR/lib/`. **BROKEN** same way.

3. **`bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs`**: exe → `<installDir>/fa`, libs → `<installDir>/lib/`. **BROKEN** same way.

That's why the uninstall deletes the grandparent ("the release layout is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Fa\bin\fa.exe`"). So Windows is fine; the POSIX layout (exe directly in the install dir) is the broken one.

So the root cause: on POSIX installs, the binary sits DIRECTLY in the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) while the native-assets runtime resolves the bundled dylib as `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` = `~/.local/lib/<name>` — but every POSIX installer copies the libs to `<exe_dir>/lib` = `~/.local/bin/lib`.

# Extract into a TEMP dir — nothing touches the install directory until the
# artifact above has passed the provenance gate.
tmp_extract="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t fa-extract)"
if ! tar -xzf "$tmp_archive" -C "$tmp_extract" 2>/dev/null; then
  err "E_ARCHIVE_CORRUPT: downloaded archive is corrupt or empty. Nothing was installed."
  rm -rf "$tmp_extract" "$tmp_archive"
  exit 1
fi
rm -f "$tmp_archive"

# macOS code-signature identity check (SEC-07 contract 3): verified BEFORE
# the binary lands in the install directory. Release CLI binaries are
# ad-hoc signed today — their provenance is the signed-checksum gate above;
# once releases carry a real Developer ID identity, set (or bake in)
# FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER to enforce the publisher identity and abort otherwise.
if [ "$os" = "macos" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -n "${FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER:-}" ]; then
  if ! codesign --verify --strict "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    err "E_CODESIGN_INVALID: the binary's code signature is invalid for release $FA_VERSION. Nothing was installed."
    rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
    exit 1
  fi
  authority="$(codesign -dv "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^Authority=//p' | head -1)"
  case "$authority" in
    # Anchored (gh-814 r2): the expected identity must PREFIX the signing
    # authority — a substring match would accept lookalike CN fragments.
    "$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER"*)
      ok "Code signature identity verified: $authority"
      ;;
    "")
      err "E_SIGNER_MISSING: expected signer '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER' but the binary carries no signature identity. Nothing was installed."
      rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
      exit 1
      ;;
    *)
      err "E_SIGNER_MISMATCH: binary signed by '$authority', expected '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER'. Nothing was installed."
      rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
fi

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

  rm -rf "$tmp_extract" "$tmp_archive"

# macOS code-signature identity check (SEC-07 contract 3): verified BEFORE
# the binary lands in the install directory. Release CLI binaries are
# ad-hoc signed today — their provenance is the signed-checksum gate above;
# once releases carry a real Developer ID identity, set (or bake in)
# FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER to enforce the publisher identity and abort otherwise.
if [ "$os" = "macos" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -n "${FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER:-}" ]; then
  if ! codesign --verify --strict "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    err "E_CODESIGN_INVALID: the binary's code signature is invalid for release $FA_VERSION. Nothing was installed."
    rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
    exit 1
  fi
  authority="$(codesign -dv "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^Authority=//p' | head -1)"
  case "$authority" in
    # Anchored (gh-814 r2): the expected identity must PREFIX the signing
    # authority — a substring match would accept lookalike CN fragments.
    "$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER"*)
      ok "Code signature identity verified: $authority"
      ;;
    "")
      err "E_SIGNER_MISSING: expected signer '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER' but the binary carries no signature identity. Nothing was installed."
      rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
      exit 1
      ;;
    *)
      err "E_SIGNER_MISMATCH: binary signed by '$authority', expected '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER'. Nothing was installed."
      rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
fi

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

1. **`site/install.sh`** (the curl installer, POSIX): `install_dir="${FA_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"`, exe → `$install_dir/fa`, libs → `$install_dir/lib/`. **BROKEN** — binary looks in `$install_dir/../lib`.

2. **`install_local.sh`** (build-from-source): `INSTALL_DIR="${INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"`, exe → `$INSTALL_DIR/fa`, libs → `$INSTALL_DIR/lib/`. **BROKEN** same way.

3. **`bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs`**: exe → `<installDir>/fa`, libs → `<installDir>/lib/`. **BROKEN** same way.

4. **`site/install.ps1`** (Windows): `$binDir = Join-Path $installDir "bin"`, exe → `$binDir\fa.exe`, libs → `$installDir\lib`. Lookup `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `$installDir\lib` — **CORRECT** already! That's why the uninstall deletes the grandparent ("the release layout is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Fa\bin\fa.exe`"). So Windows is fine; the POSIX layout (exe directly in the install dir) is the broken one.

So the root cause: on POSIX installs, the binary sits DIRECTLY in the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) while the native-assets runtime resolves the bundled dylib as `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` = `~/.local/lib/<name>` — but every POSIX installer copies the libs to `<exe_dir>/lib` = `~/.local/bin/lib`.

Two coherent fix directions:

**A. Change the POSIX installers to install the exe under a `bin/` subdir?** — No, that changes PATH semantics (`~/.local/bin` must stay on PATH; putting it in a nested `bin/` breaks the `~/.local/bin/fa` contract). Bad.

**B. Change the POSIX installers to put libs in `<install_dir>/../lib`** — matches the binary's native-assets lookup: `~/.local/bin/fa` + `../lib` = `~/.local/lib`. This is exactly the ticket's first Expected option ("Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`)").

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).
"}

Full picture now. Installers that place the binary + libs:

1. **`site/install.sh`** (the curl installer, POSIX): `install_dir="${FA_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"`, exe → `$install_dir/fa`, libs → `$install_dir/lib/`. **BROKEN** — binary looks in `$install_dir/../lib`.
   Also line 369: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "$install_dir/lib"`.

2. **`install_local.sh`** (build-from-source): `INSTALL_DIR="${INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"`, exe → `$INSTALL_DIR/fa`, libs → `$INSTALL_DIR/lib/`. **BROKEN** same way.

3. **`bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs`**: exe → `<installDir>/fa`, libs → `<installDir>/lib/`. **BROKEN** same way.

4. **`site/install.ps1`** (Windows): `$binDir = Join-Path $installDir "bin"`, exe → `$binDir\fa.exe`, libs → `$installDir\lib`. Lookup `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `$installDir\lib` — **CORRECT** already! That's why the uninstall deletes the grandparent ("the release layout is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Fa\bin\fa.exe`"). So Windows is fine; the POSIX layout (exe directly in the install dir) is the broken one.

So the root cause: on POSIX installs, the binary sits DIRECTLY in the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) while the native-assets runtime resolves the bundled dylib as `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` = `~/.local/lib/<name>` — but every POSIX installer copies the libs to `<exe_dir>/lib` = `~/.local/bin/lib`.

Two coherent fix directions:

**A. Change the POSIX installers to install the exe under a `bin/` subdir?** — No, that changes PATH semantics (`~/.local/bin` must stay on PATH; putting it in a nested `bin/` breaks the `~/.local/bin/fa` contract). Bad.

**B. Change the POSIX installers to put libs in `<install_dir>/../lib`** — matches the binary's native-assets lookup: `~/.local/bin/fa` + `../lib` = `~/.local/lib`. This is exactly the ticket's first Expected option ("Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`)").

Then:
- **Clean degradation**: the engine maps the native-assets load failure to a clean StateError (the ticket's third expectation). "Fall back to the system library" is impossible at Dart level with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (no override API; the VM resolver doesn't fall back) — so the honest implementation is the clean "sqlite unavailable" note telling the user to reinstall/update. I'll document that.

Wait — actually, let me double-check whether a system fallback is truly impossible. Hmm, one more idea: `@ffi.DefaultAsset` on the generated bindings — we can't change package code. Could we set an environment variable like `DART_NATIVE_ASSETS`? No such override. There is `DynamicLibrary.open('libsqlite3.dylib')` fallback INSIDE the VM resolver? The probe error shows only the mapped relative path attempt — single shot. Confirmed impossible without forking the package. (For the ticket's "either/or" wording, the installer fix + clean note satisfies it; the system-fallback bullet was one of several alternatives — "and/or".)

Hmm wait, actually, let me reconsider — is there really no way to preload the library? With native assets, symbols are resolved against the mapped library — `DynamicLibrary.open('/usr/libsqlite3.dylib')` on our own wouldn't help the `@ffi.Native` bindings (they resolve via the asset mapping, not a handle we hold). Correct, impossible.

**1. `site/install.sh`** — copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` instead of `$install_dir/lib`:
   - line 345: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"` → `"$lib_target"` where `lib_target="$install_dir/../lib"`... careful with `~/.local/bin/../lib` = `~/.local/lib` (fine, `..` resolution is textual in cp but works). Better compute explicitly.

**2. `install_local.sh`** — same: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"` + `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"` → `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.

**3. `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs`** — copy to `<installDir>/../lib`. BUT: Windows! On Windows, `installDir` = `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Fa\bin` (exe at `$installDir\fa.exe`)? On Windows the target is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Fa\bin\fa.exe` so installDir = `...\Fa\bin`, and the native-assets lookup is `...\Fa\lib` — the CURRENT code copies to `...\Fa\bin\lib` which is WRONG on Windows too?! But install.ps1 copies to `$installDir\lib` = `...\Fa\lib` which is RIGHT. So `fa update` on Windows would ALSO break the lookup (copies to the wrong place). Changing `_copyBundleLibs` to `<installDir>/../lib` fixes Windows `fa update` as well and unifies with install.ps1.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).
"}

Full picture now. Installers that place the binary + libs:

1. **`site/install.sh`** (the curl installer, POSIX): `install_dir="${FA_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"`, exe → `$install_dir/fa`, libs → `$install_dir/lib/`. **BROKEN** — binary looks in `$install_dir/../lib`.
   Also line 369: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "$install_dir/lib"`.

2. **`install_local.sh`** (build-from-source): `INSTALL_DIR="${INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"`, exe → `$INSTALL_DIR/fa`, libs → `$INSTALL_DIR/lib/`. **BROKEN** same way.

3. **`bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs`**: exe → `<installDir>/fa`, libs → `<installDir>/lib/`. **BROKEN** same way.

4. **`site/install.ps1`** (Windows): `$binDir = Join-Path $installDir "bin"`, exe → `$binDir\fa.exe`, libs → `$installDir\lib`. Lookup `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `$installDir\lib` — **CORRECT** already! That's why the uninstall deletes the grandparent ("the release layout is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Fa\bin\fa.exe`"). So Windows is fine; the POSIX layout (exe directly in the install dir) is the broken one.

So the root cause: on POSIX installs, the binary sits DIRECTLY in the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) while the native-assets runtime resolves the bundled dylib as `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` = `~/.local/lib/<name>` — but every POSIX installer copies the libs to `<exe_dir>/lib` = `~/.local/bin/lib`.

Two coherent fix directions:

**A. Change the POSIX installers to install the exe under a `bin/` subdir?** — No, that changes PATH semantics (`~/.local/bin` must stay on PATH; putting it in a nested `bin/` breaks the `~/.local/bin/fa` contract). Bad.

**B. Change the POSIX installers to put libs in `<install_dir>/../lib`** — matches the binary's native-assets lookup: `~/.local/bin/fa` + `../lib` = `~/.local/lib`. This is exactly the ticket's first Expected option ("Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`)").

Then:
- **Clean degradation**: the engine maps the native-assets load failure to a clean StateError (the ticket's third expectation). "Fall back to the system library" is impossible at Dart level with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (no override API; the VM resolver doesn't fall back) — so the honest implementation is the clean "sqlite unavailable" note telling the user to reinstall/update. I'll document that.

Wait — actually, let me double-check whether a system fallback is truly impossible. Hmm, one more idea: `@ffi.DefaultAsset` on the generated bindings — we can't change package code. Could we set an environment variable like `DART_NATIVE_ASSETS`? No such override. There is `DynamicLibrary.open('libsqlite3.dylib')` fallback INSIDE the VM resolver? The probe error shows only the mapped relative path attempt — single shot. Confirmed impossible without forking the package. (For the ticket's "either/or" wording, the installer fix + clean note satisfies it; the system-fallback bullet was one of several alternatives — "and/or".)

Hmm wait, actually, let me reconsider — is there really no way to preload the library? With native assets, symbols are resolved against the mapped library — `DynamicLibrary.open('/usr/libsqlite3.dylib')` on our own wouldn't help the `@ffi.Native` bindings (they resolve via the asset mapping, not a handle we hold). Correct, impossible.

So final fix plan:

**1. `site/install.sh`** — copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` instead of `$install_dir/lib`:
   - line 345: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"` → `"$lib_target"` where `lib_target="$install_dir/../lib"`... careful with `~/.local/bin/../lib` = `~/.local/lib` (fine, `..` resolution is textual in cp but works). Better compute explicitly.
   - line 353-354: `cp -r ... "$install_dir/lib/"` → new target.
   - line 369: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "$install_dir/lib"` → new target.
   Also the source-run fallback instructions at line 213-214: `cp build/out/bundle/bin/fah ~/.local/bin/fa` — add `cp -r build/out/bundle/lib ~/.local/lib/`? That's an advisory string; update it to keep the layout contract visible. Let me read the whole file section first.

**2. `install_local.sh`** — same: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"` + `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"` → `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.

**3. `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs`** — copy to `<installDir>/../lib`. BUT: Windows! On Windows, `installDir` = `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Fa\bin` (exe at `$installDir\fa.exe`)? Wait no — check: `_binaryUpdate`: `target = install.executable`; `installDir = File(target).parent`. On Windows the target is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Fa\bin\fa.exe` so installDir = `...\Fa\bin`, and the native-assets lookup is `...\Fa\lib` — the CURRENT code copies to `...\Fa\bin\lib` which is WRONG on Windows too?! But install.ps1 copies to `$installDir\lib` = `...\Fa\lib` which is RIGHT. So `fa update` on Windows would ALSO break the lookup (copies to the wrong place). Changing `_copyBundleLibs` to `<installDir>/../lib` fixes Windows `fa update` as well and unifies with install.ps1. 

   Edge: what if installDir has no parent (root)? `Directory('${installDir.parent.path}/lib')` — installDir is never filesystem root realistically (`/fa`?). installDir.parent of `/` is `/` — fine.

Leave old files — harmless, uninstall doesn't remove them either (non-Windows uninstall only removes the binary). Not in scope; don't add risk. Hmm — but a stale broken copy at `~/.local/bin/lib` stays; it's inert. Ticket doesn't ask for cleanup. Skip.

Engine clean degradation** (`lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`): wrap `sqlite3.open` → catch `ArgumentError` (the ffi resolver's load failure shape: message contains "Failed to load dynamic library") → throw `StateError` with a clean "SQLite is unavailable" message explaining the bundled lib couldn't be loaded at `<exe_dir>/../lib` and to re-run the installer / `fa update`. Let me be precise: classify ONLY messages containing 'Failed to load dynamic library' or "Couldn't resolve native function").

Make `copyBundleLibs` public (rename from `_copyBundleLibs`, following `extractArchive`'s "public for tests" pattern).

Test the public behavior: feed the exact error strings (from the ticket + the probe) through the classifier and through `openReadOnly`'s wrapper. For `openReadOnly` I need a seam to simulate the throw — e.g. expose a `SqliteOpen` function hook? Minimal: extract `classifySqliteUnavailableError(Object error) → String?` (pure) + `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` uses it in its catch. Unit-test the classifier with the three real error shapes; ALSO an end-to-end test that `read` on a `.db` in an environment WITHOUT the lib produces the clean note... can't simulate in-process. So classifier tests + a small test asserting the engine surfaces the clean message when open throws a load-shaped ArgumentError — via a tiny injectable: `Sqlite3Engine({SqliteDatabase Function(String path)? openImpl})`? Hmm — that changes the constructor... Actually `const Sqlite3Engine()` is used in `bin/fah_runapp.dart` (`sqliteEngine: const Sqlite3Engine()`). I could add an optional `@visibleForTesting openOverride`. Let me look at how the repo usually tests ffi seams... e.g. shift_hid has seams (`ownProcessGroupOverride`). ok "Archive checksum verified."
[ "$trust_pem" = "${FA_SIGNING_PEM:-}" ] || rm -f "$trust_pem"

# dart build cli produces a bundle/ dir: bundle/bin/fa + bundle/lib/*.dylib
# Extract into a TEMP dir — nothing touches the install directory until the
# artifact above has passed the provenance gate.
tmp_extract="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t fa-extract)"
if ! tar -xzf "$tmp_archive" -C "$tmp_extract" 2>/dev/null; then
  err "E_ARCHIVE_CORRUPT: downloaded archive is corrupt or empty. Nothing was installed."
  rm -rf "$tmp_extract" "$tmp_archive"
  exit 1
fi
rm -f "$tmp_archive"

# macOS code-signature identity check (SEC-07 contract 3): verified BEFORE
# the binary lands in the install directory. Release CLI binaries are
# ad-hoc signed today — their provenance is the signed-checksum gate above;
# once releases carry a real Developer ID identity, set (or bake in)
# FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER to enforce the publisher identity and abort otherwise.
if [ "$os" = "macos" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -n "${FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER:-}" ]; then
  if ! codesign --verify --strict "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    err "E_CODESIGN_INVALID: the binary's code signature is invalid for release $FA_VERSION. Nothing was installed."
    rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
    exit 1
  fi
  authority="$(codesign -dv "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^Authority=//p' | head -1)"
  case "$authority" in
    # Anchored (gh-814 r2): the expected identity must PREFIX the signing
    # authority — a substring match would accept lookalike CN fragments.
    "$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER"*)
      ok "Code signature identity verified: $authority"
      ;;
    "")
      err "E_SIGNER_MISSING: expected signer '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER' but the binary carries no signature identity. Nothing was installed."
      rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
      exit 1
      ;;
    *)
      err "E_SIGNER_MISMATCH: binary signed by '$authority', expected '$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER'. Nothing was installed."
      rm -rf "$tmp_extract"
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
fi

mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"
rm -f "$target"  # break any pre-existing symlink so cp writes the real file
cp "$tmp_extract/bundle/bin/fa" "$target"
chmod +x "$target"
# Copy version.txt so the binary can report its version.
if [ -f "$tmp_extract/bundle/version.txt" ]; then
  cp "$tmp_extract/bundle/version.txt" "$install_dir/version.txt"
fi
if [ -d "$tmp_extract/bundle/lib" ]; then
  cp -r "$tmp_extract/bundle/lib/"* "$install_dir/lib/" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
rm -rf "$tmp_extract"

ok "Installed $target"

# macOS quarantine / signature hardening — runs ONLY after the provenance
# gate above succeeded (SEC-07 #795: no blind quarantine strip). Downloaded

# the quarantine attribute is removed. Re-signing ad-hoc makes the binary
# runnable from any directory on Apple Silicon, even without a paid
# Developer ID certificate.
if [ "$os" = "macos" ]; then
  if command -v xattr >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "$target" 2>/dev/null || true
    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "$install_dir/lib" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  if command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    codesign --force --sign - "$target" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
fi

# ── 5. Ensure install directory is on PATH ───────────────────────────────────
if command -v fa >/dev/null 2>&1 || command -v fah >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ok "'fa' is on PATH ($(command -v fa 2>/dev/null || command -v fah))."
else
  warn "'fa' is not on PATH yet. The executable lives in $install_dir"
  say ""

  shell_rc=""
  case "${SHELL:-}" in
    */zsh)  shell_rc="$HOME/.zshrc" ;;
    */bash) shell_rc="$HOME/.bashrc" ;;
    */fish) shell_rc="$HOME/.config/fish/config.fish" ;;
  esac

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: On installed `fa` binaries (POSIX), the builtin `read` tool on any `.db`/`.sqlite` file fails with a raw FFI error: `Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)`.

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite through Dart **native assets** (`DynamicLoadingBundled`). An AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<libname>` (bundle layout: `bundle/bin/fa` + `bundle/lib/*.dylib`). Every POSIX installer copies the executable DIRECTLY into the install dir (`~/.local/bin/fa`) but copies the bundle libs into `<install_dir>/lib/` (`~/.local/bin/lib/`):

- `site/install.sh` (lines ~345/353: `mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"`, `cp -r … "$install_dir/lib/"`)
- `install_local.sh` (lines ~20/70: `mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/lib"`, `cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/lib/"`)
- `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` (copies `bundle/lib/*` to `<installDir>/lib`)

The native-assets resolver therefore looks at `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` and finds nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` symbol call throws an unclassified `ArgumentError` that the `read` tool surfaces as a raw FFI dump. Verified empirically: relocating a `dart build cli` binary so the lib sits at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` loads fine; with the installer layout it fails with exactly the reported error. Windows `site/install.ps1` is already correct (it installs the exe into `<root>\bin\`, so `<exe_dir>\..\lib` = `<root>\lib` = its lib target) — but `fa update` (`_copyBundleLibs`) would break Windows installs too (it targets `<root>\bin\lib`).

**Impact**: every binary install of `fa` on macOS/Linux cannot use SQLite reads (`read path=x.db…`); it only worked on machines with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. `fa update` propagates the broken layout on every update.

**Fix approach**:
1. Install the bundle libs where the binary's native-assets resolver looks — `<install_dir>/../lib` — in all three places (`site/install.sh`, `install_local.sh`, `self_manage` `copyBundleLibs`). This also aligns `fa update` with `install.ps1` on Windows (`<root>\lib`).
2. Clean degradation in the FFI engine (`Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly`): a dynamic-library load failure (`ArgumentError` from the dart:ffi resolver) becomes a clean `StateError` "SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`" — the same clean-error channel the tool uses when no engine is wired, instead of a raw FFI dump. A Dart-level fallback to the system sqlite library is not possible with package:sqlite3 3.x native assets (the `@ffi.Native` bindings resolve via the build-time asset mapping; there is no loader-override API), so a repaired install layout is the fix.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development round).

The implementation works (the StateError with the clean note IS thrown — the test failure is just my `expect(engine.openReadOnly(...), throwsA(...))` pattern: `openReadOnly` is NOT a Future, it's synchronous — `expect(syncFn(), throwsA(...))` executes the function immediately and the exception escapes before expect can catch. Need `Directory('${bundle.path}/lib').createSync(recursive: true)` before writing files. My test wrote `File('${bundle.path}/libsqlite3.dylib').writeAsStringSync('dylib')` without creating the lib subdir. Fix the test.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` / `--timer`/`--deadline` / `/timer` write one
  session clock, the per-turn context carries a `time-left:` line while
  armed, and one-shot system notices steer wrap-up at ~50%, T-3min
  (drain background jobs), and T-30s; absent deadline = byte-for-byte
  today's behavior.

bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

  today's behavior.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per

  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` / `--timer`/`--deadline` / `/timer` write one
  session clock, the per-turn context carries a `time-left:` line while
  armed, and one-shot system notices steer wrap-up at ~50%, T-3min
  (drain background jobs), and T-30s; absent deadline = byte-for-byte
  today's behavior.

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

# Changelog

bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

arguments.newText:
## Unreleased

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.

bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full

  today's behavior.

No further doc updates needed. Adding the changelog entry:

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.","oldText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.","path":"CHANGELOG.md"}

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).

  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with

bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full

  today's behavior.

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.","oldText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.","path":"CHANGELOG.md"}

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` / `--timer`/`--deadline` / `/timer` write one
  session clock, the per-turn context carries a `time-left:` line while
  armed, and one-shot system notices steer wrap-up at ~50%, T-3min
  (drain background jobs), and T-30s; absent deadline = byte-for-byte
  today's behavior.

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.","oldText":"## Unreleased

          echo "rehearsing the stamp of the NEXT tag: v$next"
          bash scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage "$next"
          # The staged tree must ANALYZE clean: v0.1.411 shipped files
          # with broken imports (the staging filter pruned lib/src/memory;
          # imports of fork-only dart_tui symbols) that only a consumer's
          # `dart analyze` ever surfaced (issue #613). Errors fail the
          # gate; warnings/infos pass, matching the static analyze stage.
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub get && dart analyze)
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:

bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under

publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).

bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).
