# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` / `--timer`/`--deadline` / `/timer` write one
  session clock, the per-turn context carries a `time-left:` line while
  armed, and one-shot system notices steer wrap-up at ~50%, T-3min
  (drain background jobs), and T-30s; absent deadline = byte-for-byte
  today's behavior.

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.","oldText":"## Unreleased

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every

  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with

Need `Directory('${bundle.path}/lib').createSync(recursive: true)` before writing files. My test wrote `File('${bundle.path}/libsqlite3.dylib').writeAsStringSync('dylib')` without creating the lib subdir. Fix the test.

bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.","oldText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.","path":"CHANGELOG.md"}

The implementation works (the StateError with the clean note IS thrown — the test failure is just my `expect(engine.openReadOnly(...), throwsA(...))` pattern: `openReadOnly` is NOT a Future, it's synchronous — `expect(syncFn(), throwsA(...))` executes the function immediately and the exception escapes before expect can catch. Need `Directory('${bundle.path}/lib').createSync(recursive: true)` before writing files. My test wrote `File('${bundle.path}/libsqlite3.dylib').writeAsStringSync('dylib')` without creating the lib subdir. Fix the test.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out

CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.","oldText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.","path":"CHANGELOG.md"}

The implementation works (the StateError with the clean note IS thrown — the test failure is just my `expect(engine.openReadOnly(...), throwsA(...))` pattern: `openReadOnly` is NOT a Future, it's synchronous — `expect(syncFn(), throwsA(...))` executes the function immediately and the exception escapes before expect can catch. I need `expect(() => engine.openReadOnly(path), throwsA(...))` — a closure. Same for the non-load rethrow test and the self_manage test PathNotFound issues.

The two `copyBundleLibs` test failures: `PathNotFoundException: Cannot open file, path = '.../bundle/libsqlite3.dylib'` at `File(...).writeAsStringSync` — because I created the parent `bundle` dir but not `bundle/lib`. Need `Directory('${bundle.path}/lib').createSync(recursive: true)` before writing files. My test wrote `File('${bundle.path}/libsqlite3.dylib').writeAsStringSync('dylib')` without creating the lib subdir. Fix the test.

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary

  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` / `--timer`/`--deadline` / `/timer` write one
  session clock, the per-turn context carries a `time-left:` line while
  armed, and one-shot system notices steer wrap-up at ~50%, T-3min
  (drain background jobs), and T-30s; absent deadline = byte-for-byte
  today's behavior.

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).

blocks.text:
# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.","oldText":"## Unreleased

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.","oldText":"## Unreleased

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.","oldText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.","path":"CHANGELOG.md"}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

grep -qF 'latest|v*)' "$INSTALLER" || {
  echo "FAIL (contract1): no v-prefix normalization for FA_VERSION"; exit 1
}
echo "ok  (contract1): installer defaults to the vpinned marker; latest is opt-in; bare pins normalize to v-tags"

# ── marker resolution through the real installer (contract 1b) ──────────────
# Default install (no FA_VERSION) must resolve vpinned/PINNED_VERSION from
# the SAME fixture base and install the marked release.
run_install_default() { # run_install_default <fixture-dir>; no FA_VERSION
  rm -rf "$install_dir"; mkdir -p "$install_dir"
  (cd "$work" &&
    FA_INSTALL_DIR="$install_dir" \
    FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL="file://$1" \
    FA_SIGNING_PEM="$work/test.pub" \
    PATH="$shim:$PATH" \
    sh "$INSTALLER" > "$work/out-default.log" 2>&1
  )
}
mkdir -p "$fixture/vpinned"
printf 'v0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/vpinned/PINNED_VERSION"
if ! run_install_default "$fixture"; then
  echo "FAIL (contract1b): default install via marker failed:"; cat "$work/out-default.log"; exit 1
fi
grep -q "Pinned marker resolves to: v0.0.0-test" "$work/out-default.log" || {
  echo "FAIL (contract1b): marker resolution not logged:"; cat "$work/out-default.log"; exit 1
}
[ -x "$install_dir/fa" ] || { echo "FAIL (contract1b): resolved install left no binary"; exit 1; }

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.","oldText":"## Unreleased

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall/`fa update`` note instead of the
  raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible with
  package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override).

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.","oldText":"## Unreleased

#!/usr/bin/env bash

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

#!/usr/bin/env bash

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

#!/usr/bin/env bash

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

#!/usr/bin/env bash

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the install…

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-library fallback is not possible with native-assets bindings (build-time asset mapping, no loader override).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine_stub.dart`: constructor parity for the conditional export.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` — new `missing bundled library degrades cleanly (gh-1574)` group: load-failure classification (macOS + Linux error shapes), clean-note mapping through `openReadOnly` and through the `read` tool, non-load errors unclassified.
- `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` — `copyBundleLibs` installs into `<installDir>/../lib` and never `<installDir>/lib`; static layout contract for `install_local.sh`, `site/install.sh`, and `site/install.ps1`.
- Targeted suites: 85 tests passed (`sqlite_engine_test` + `self_manage_test`), all previously failing repro tests now green.
- Full suite: SEE_SUITE_RESULT
- `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` (AC1–AC4): unchanged behavior — one pre-existing `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit (environment-specific, not touched by this fix).

### Notes

- Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update` (both now write the correct layout). Stale libs at `~/.local/bin/lib` are inert leftovers; nothing reads them.
- Windows `site/install.ps1` needed no change; its layout (`<root>\bin\fa.exe` + `<root>\lib`) already matches the native-assets lookup.
- Release archives are unchanged (`bundle/bin` + `bundle/lib`) — only install destinations moved.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"content":"### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-library fallback is not possible with native-assets bindings (build-time asset mapping, no loader override).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine_stub.dart`: constructor parity for the conditional export.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` — new `missing bundled library degrades cleanly (gh-1574)` group: load-failure classification (macOS + Linux error shapes), clean-note mapping through `openReadOnly` and through the `read` tool, non-load errors unclassified.
- `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` — `copyBundleLibs` installs into `<installDir>/../lib` and never `<installDir>/lib`; static layout contract for `install_local.sh`, `site/install.sh`, and `site/install.ps1`.
- Targeted suites: 85 tests passed (`sqlite_engine_test` + `self_manage_test`), all previously failing repro tests now green.
- Full suite: SEE_SUITE_RESULT
- `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` (AC1–AC4): unchanged behavior — one pre-existing `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit (environment-specific, not touched by this fix).

### Notes

- Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update` (both now write the correct layout). Stale libs at `~/.local/bin/lib` are inert leftovers; nothing reads them.
- Windows `site/install.ps1` needed no change; its layout (`<root>\bin\fa.exe` + `<root>\lib`) already matches the native-assets lookup.
- Release archives are unchanged (`bundle/bin` + `bundle/lib`) — only install destinations moved.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"content":"### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle
