{"content":"### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-library fallback is not possible with native-assets bindings (build-time asset mapping, no loader override).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine_stub.dart`: constructor parity for the conditional export.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` — new `missing bundled library degrades cleanly (gh-1574)` group: load-failure classification (macOS + Linux error shapes), clean-note mapping through `openReadOnly` and through the `read` tool, non-load errors unclassified.
- `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` — `copyBundleLibs` installs into `<installDir>/../lib` and never `<installDir>/lib`; static layout contract for `install_local.sh`, `site/install.sh`, and `site/install.ps1`.
- Targeted suites: 85 tests passed (`sqlite_engine_test` + `self_manage_test`), all previously failing repro tests now green.
- Full suite: SEE_SUITE_RESULT
- `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` (AC1–AC4): unchanged behavior — one pre-existing `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit (environment-specific, not touched by this fix).

### Notes

- Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update` (both now write the correct layout). Stale libs at `~/.local/bin/lib` are inert leftovers; nothing reads them.
- Windows `site/install.ps1` needed no change; its layout (`<root>\bin\fa.exe` + `<root>\lib`) already matches the native-assets lookup.
- Release archives are unchanged (`bundle/bin` + `bundle/lib`) — only install destinations moved.

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"content":"### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-library fallback is not possible with native-assets bindings (build-time asset mapping, no loader override).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine_stub.dart`: constructor parity for the conditional export.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` — new `missing bundled library degrades cleanly (gh-1574)` group: load-failure classification (macOS + Linux error shapes), clean-note mapping through `openReadOnly` and through the `read` tool, non-load errors unclassified.
- `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` — `copyBundleLibs` installs into `<installDir>/../lib` and never `<installDir>/lib`; static layout contract for `install_local.sh`, `site/install.sh`, and `site/install.ps1`.
- Targeted suites: 85 tests passed (`sqlite_engine_test` + `self_manage_test`), all previously failing repro tests now green.
- Full suite: SEE_SUITE_RESULT
- `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` (AC1–AC4): unchanged behavior — one pre-existing `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit (environment-specific, not touched by this fix).

### Notes

- Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update` (both now write the correct layout). Stale libs at `~/.local/bin/lib` are inert leftovers; nothing reads them.
- Windows `site/install.ps1` needed no change; its layout (`<root>\bin\fa.exe` + `<root>\lib`) already matches the native-assets lookup.
- Release archives are unchanged (`bundle/bin` + `bundle/lib`) — only install destinations moved.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the install…

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"content":"### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-library fallback is not possible with native-assets bindings (build-time asset mapping, no loader override).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine_stub.dart`: constructor parity for the conditional export.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` — new `missing bundled library degrades cleanly (gh-1574)` group: load-failure classification (macOS + Linux error shapes), clean-note mapping through `openReadOnly` and through the `read` tool, non-load errors unclassified.
- `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` — `copyBundleLibs` installs into `<installDir>/../lib` and never `<installDir>/lib`; static layout contract for `install_local.sh`, `site/install.sh`, and `site/install.ps1`.
- Targeted suites: 85 tests passed (`sqlite_engine_test` + `self_manage_test`), all previously failing repro tests now green.
- Full suite: SEE_SUITE_RESULT
- `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` (AC1–AC4): unchanged behavior — one pre-existing `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit (environment-specific, not touched by this fix).

### Notes

- Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update` (both now write the correct layout). Stale libs at `~/.local/bin/lib` are inert leftovers; nothing reads them.
- Windows `site/install.ps1` needed no change; its layout (`<root>\bin\fa.exe` + `<root>\lib`) already matches the native-assets lookup.
- Release archives are unchanged (`bundle/bin` + `bundle/lib`) — only install destinations moved.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"content":"### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-library fallback is not possible with native-assets bindings (build-time asset mapping, no loader override).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine_stub.dart`: constructor parity for the conditional export.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` — new `missing bundled library degrades cleanly (gh-1574)` group: load-failure classification (macOS + Linux error shapes), clean-note mapping through `openReadOnly` and through the `read` tool, non-load errors unclassified.
- `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` — `copyBundleLibs` installs into `<installDir>/../lib` and never `<installDir>/lib`; static layout contract for `install_local.sh`, `site/install.sh`, and `site/install.ps1`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"content":"### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-library fallback is not possible with native-assets bindings (build-time asset mapping, no loader override).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine_stub.dart`: constructor parity for the conditional export.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` — new `missing bundled library degrades cleanly (gh-1574)` group: load-failure classification (macOS + Linux error shapes), clean-note mapping through `openReadOnly` and through the `read` tool, non-load errors unclassified.
- `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` — `copyBundleLibs` installs into `<installDir>/../lib` and never `<installDir>/lib`; static layout contract for `install_local.sh`, `site/install.sh`, and `site/install.ps1`.
- Targeted suites: 85 tests passed (`sqlite_engine_test` + `self_manage_test`), all previously failing repro tests now green.
- Full suite: SEE_SUITE_RESULT
- `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` (AC1–AC4): unchanged behavior — one pre-existing `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit (environment-specific, not touched by this fix).

### Notes

- Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update` (both now write the correct layout). Stale libs at `~/.local/bin/lib` are inert leftovers; nothing reads them.
- Windows `site/install.ps1` needed no change; its layout (`<root>\bin\fa.exe` + `<root>\lib`) already matches the native-assets lookup.
- Release archives are unchanged (`bundle/bin` + `bundle/lib`) — only install destinations moved.

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow
    detection via error-message regexes.
  - **Invariant to preserve: providers never throw.** All failures —
    network, 429, abort, malformed SSE — arrive as an `error` event with
    `stopReason: error|aborted`. The agent loop never sees an exception from
    a provider.
- `packages/agent/` (~8.1k LOC TS):
  - `packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts` (748 LOC) — the low-level async loop;
    port its shape, not its incidental JS-isms.
  - `packages/agent/src/agent.ts` (557 LOC) — stateful `Agent` with
    **steering / follow-up queues** (inject user messages mid-run — this is

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"content":"### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-library fallback is not possible with native-assets bindings (build-time asset mapping, no loader override).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine_stub.dart`: constructor parity for the conditional export.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` — new `missing bundled library degrades cleanly (gh-1574)` group: load-failure classification (macOS + Linux error shapes), clean-note mapping through `openReadOnly` and through the `read` tool, non-load errors unclassified.
- `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` — `copyBundleLibs` installs into `<installDir>/../lib` and never `<installDir>/lib`; static layout contract for `install_local.sh`, `site/install.sh`, and `site/install.ps1`.
- Targeted suites: 85 tests passed (`sqlite_engine_test` + `self_manage_test`), all previously failing repro tests now green.
- Full suite: SEE_SUITE_RESULT
- `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` (AC1–AC4): unchanged behavior — one pre-existing `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit (environment-specific, not touched by this fix).

### Notes

- Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update` (both now write the correct layout). Stale libs at `~/.local/bin/lib` are inert leftovers; nothing reads them.
- Windows `site/install.ps1` needed no change; its layout (`<root>\bin\fa.exe` + `<root>\lib`) already matches the native-assets lookup.
- Release archives are unchanged (`bundle/bin` + `bundle/lib`) — only install destinations moved.

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"content":"### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-library fallback is not possible with native-assets bindings (build-time asset mapping, no loader override).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine_stub.dart`: constructor parity for the conditional export.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` — new `missing bundled library degrades cleanly (gh-1574)` group: load-failure classification (macOS + Linux error shapes), clean-note mapping through `openReadOnly` and through the `read` tool, non-load errors unclassified.
- `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` — `copyBundleLibs` installs into `<installDir>/../lib` and never `<installDir>/lib`; static layout contract for `install_local.sh`, `site/install.sh`, and `site/install.ps1`.
- Targeted suites: 85 tests passed (`sqlite_engine_test` + `self_manage_test`), all previously failing repro tests now green.
- Full suite: SEE_SUITE_RESULT
- `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` (AC1–AC4): unchanged behavior — one pre-existing `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit (environment-specific, not touched by this fix).

### Notes

- Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update` (both now write the correct layout). Stale libs at `~/.local/bin/lib` are inert leftovers; nothing reads them.
- Windows `site/install.ps1` needed no change; its layout (`<root>\bin\fa.exe` + `<root>\lib`) already matches the native-assets lookup.
- Release archives are unchanged (`bundle/bin` + `bundle/lib`) — only install destinations moved.

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow
    detection via error-message regexes.
  - **Invariant to preserve: providers never throw.** All failures —
    network, 429, abort, malformed SSE — arrive as an `error` event with
    `stopReason: error|aborted`. The agent loop never sees an exception from

# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"content":"### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-library fallback is not possible with native-assets bindings (build-time asset mapping, no loader override).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine_stub.dart`: constructor parity for the conditional export.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` — new `missing bundled library degrades cleanly (gh-1574)` group: load-failure classification (macOS + Linux error shapes), clean-note mapping through `openReadOnly` and through the `read` tool, non-load errors unclassified.
- `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` — `copyBundleLibs` installs into `<installDir>/../lib` and never `<installDir>/lib`; static layout contract for `install_local.sh`, `site/install.sh`, and `site/install.ps1`.
- Targeted suites: 85 tests passed (`sqlite_engine_test` + `self_manage_test`), all previously failing repro tests now green.
- Full suite: SEE_SUITE_RESULT
- `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` (AC1–AC4): unchanged behavior — one pre-existing `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit (environment-specific, not touched by this fix).

### Notes

- Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update` (both now write the correct layout). Stale libs at `~/.local/bin/lib` are inert leftovers; nothing reads them.
- Windows `site/install.ps1` needed no change; its layout (`<root>\bin\fa.exe` + `<root>\lib`) already matches the native-assets lookup.
- Release archives are unchanged (`bundle/bin` + `bundle/lib`) — only install destinations moved.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"content":"### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-library fallback is not possible with native-assets bindings (build-time asset mapping, no loader override).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine_stub.dart`: constructor parity for the conditional export.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` — new `missing bundled library degrades cleanly (gh-1574)` group: load-failure classification (macOS + Linux error shapes), clean-note mapping through `openReadOnly` and through the `read` tool, non-load errors unclassified.
- `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` — `copyBundleLibs` installs into `<installDir>/../lib` and never `<installDir>/lib`; static layout contract for `install_local.sh`, `site/install.sh`, and `site/install.ps1`.
- Targeted suites: 85 tests passed (`sqlite_engine_test` + `self_manage_test`), all previously failing repro tests now green.
- Full suite: SEE_SUITE_RESULT
- `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` (AC1–AC4): unchanged behavior — one pre-existing `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit (environment-specific, not touched by this fix).

### Notes

- Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update` (both now write the correct layout). Stale libs at `~/.local/bin/lib` are inert leftovers; nothing reads them.
- Windows `site/install.ps1` needed no change; its layout (`<root>\bin\fa.exe` + `<root>\lib`) already matches the native-assets lookup.
- Release archives are unchanged (`bundle/bin` + `bundle/lib`) — only install destinations moved.

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow
    detection via error-message regexes.
  - **Invariant to preserve: providers never throw.** All failures —
    network, 429, abort, malformed SSE — arrive as an `error` event with
    `stopReason: error|aborted`. The agent loop never sees an exception from
    a provider.
- `packages/agent/` (~8.1k LOC TS):
  - `packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts` (748 LOC) — the low-level async loop;
    port its shape, not its incidental JS-isms.
  - `packages/agent/src/agent.ts` (557 LOC) — stateful `Agent` with
    **steering / follow-up queues** (inject user messages mid-run — this is

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"content":"### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-library fallback is not possible with native-assets bindings (build-time asset mapping, no loader override).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine_stub.dart`: constructor parity for the conditional export.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` — new `missing bundled library degrades cleanly (gh-1574)` group: load-failure classification (macOS + Linux error shapes), clean-note mapping through `openReadOnly` and through the `read` tool, non-load errors unclassified.
- `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` — `copyBundleLibs` installs into `<installDir>/../lib` and never `<installDir>/lib`; static layout contract for `install_local.sh`, `site/install.sh`, and `site/install.ps1`.
- Targeted suites: 85 tests passed (`sqlite_engine_test` + `self_manage_test`), all previously failing repro tests now green.
- Full suite: SEE_SUITE_RESULT
- `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` (AC1–AC4): unchanged behavior — one pre-existing `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit (environment-specific, not touched by this fix).

### Notes

- Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update` (both now write the correct layout). Stale libs at `~/.local/bin/lib` are inert leftovers; nothing reads them.
- Windows `site/install.ps1` needed no change; its layout (`<root>\bin\fa.exe` + `<root>\lib`) already matches the native-assets lookup.
- Release archives are unchanged (`bundle/bin` + `bundle/lib`) — only install destinations moved.

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"content":"### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-library fallback is not possible with native-assets bindings (build-time asset mapping, no loader override).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine_stub.dart`: constructor parity for the conditional export.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` — new `missing bundled library degrades cleanly (gh-1574)` group: load-failure classification (macOS + Linux error shapes), clean-note mapping through `openReadOnly` and through the `read` tool, non-load errors unclassified.
- `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` — `copyBundleLibs` installs into `<installDir>/../lib` and never `<installDir>/lib`; static layout contract for `install_local.sh`, `site/install.sh`, and `site/install.ps1`.
- Targeted suites: 85 tests passed (`sqlite_engine_test` + `self_manage_test`), all previously failing repro tests now green.
- Full suite: SEE_SUITE_RESULT
- `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` (AC1–AC4): unchanged behavior — one pre-existing `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit (environment-specific, not touched by this fix).

### Notes

- Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update` (both now write the correct layout). Stale libs at `~/.local/bin/lib` are inert leftovers; nothing reads them.
- Windows `site/install.ps1` needed no change; its layout (`<root>\bin\fa.exe` + `<root>\lib`) already matches the native-assets lookup.
- Release archives are unchanged (`bundle/bin` + `bundle/lib`) — only install destinations moved.

imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"content":"### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-library fallback is not possible with native-assets bindings (build-time asset mapping, no loader override).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine_stub.dart`: constructor parity for the conditional export.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` — new `missing bundled library degrades cleanly (gh-1574)` group: load-failure classification (macOS + Linux error shapes), clean-note mapping through `openReadOnly` and through the `read` tool, non-load errors unclassified.
- `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` — `copyBundleLibs` installs into `<installDir>/../lib` and never `<installDir>/lib`; static layout contract for `install_local.sh`, `site/install.sh`, and `site/install.ps1`.
- Targeted suites: 85 tests passed (`sqlite_engine_test` + `self_manage_test`), all previously failing repro tests now green.
- Full suite: SEE_SUITE_RESULT
- `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` (AC1–AC4): unchanged behavior — one pre-existing `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit (environment-specific, not touched by this fix).

### Notes

- Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update` (both now write the correct layout). Stale libs at `~/.local/bin/lib` are inert leftovers; nothing reads them.
- Windows `site/install.ps1` needed no change; its layout (`<root>\bin\fa.exe` + `<root>\lib`) already matches the native-assets lookup.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

{"content":"### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-library fallback is not possible with native-assets bindings (build-time asset mapping, no loader override).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine_stub.dart`: constructor parity for the conditional export.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` — new `missing bundled library degrades cleanly (gh-1574)` group: load-failure classification (macOS + Linux error shapes), clean-note mapping through `openReadOnly` and through the `read` tool, non-load errors unclassified.
- `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` — `copyBundleLibs` installs into `<installDir>/../lib` and never `<installDir>/lib`; static layout contract for `install_local.sh`, `site/install.sh`, and `site/install.ps1`.
- Targeted suites: 85 tests passed (`sqlite_engine_test` + `self_manage_test`), all previously failing repro tests now green.
- Full suite: SEE_SUITE_RESULT
- `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` (AC1–AC4): unchanged behavior — one pre-existing `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit (environment-specific, not touched by this fix).

### Notes

- Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update` (both now write the correct layout). Stale libs at `~/.local/bin/lib` are inert leftovers; nothing reads them.
- Windows `site/install.ps1` needed no change; its layout (`<root>\bin\fa.exe` + `<root>\lib`) already matches the native-assets lookup.
- Release archives are unchanged (`bundle/bin` + `bundle/lib`) — only install destinations moved.

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,

imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle
