blocks.text:
# weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

# weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

Everything is committed to the branch and `outputs/response.md` is written. The task is complete:

**gh-1574 — SQLite reads failing on installed `fa` binaries: fixed.**

**Root cause** (verified empirically with a real `dart build cli` bundle): `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart native assets — the AOT binary resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`, but every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary (`<install_dir>/lib`). For `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error.

**Fix (TDD — repro tests written first, confirmed failing):**
- Installers now write the libs where the binary looks (`<install_dir>/../lib`): `site/install.sh` (incl. the macOS quarantine-xattr pass + source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update` (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, made public and layout-pinned; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct).
- `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` degrades a library-load failure to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` / `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in the pure core) instead of the raw FFI dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-lib fallback is impossible with native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader override) — documented in the RCA.

**Verification:**
- Repro tests now green: `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` (classification + clean-note through the engine and the `read` tool), `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` (installer layout contract, incl. static assertions on both shell installers) — 119 targeted tests pass.
- Full CI-scope suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration,browser-ext`): **10,547 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures**.
- `dart analyze lib test bin`: no errors/warnings; `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` AC1–AC4 unchanged (one `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit — pre-existing, environment-specific).
- End-to-end proof: a relocated real native-assets binary with the new layout loads SQLite successfully.

# weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

**gh-1574 — SQLite reads failing on installed `fa` binaries: fixed.**

**Root cause** (verified empirically with a real `dart build cli` bundle): `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart native assets — the AOT binary resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`, but every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary (`<install_dir>/lib`). For `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error.

**Fix (TDD — repro tests written first, confirmed failing):**
- Installers now write the libs where the binary looks (`<install_dir>/../lib`): `site/install.sh` (incl. the macOS quarantine-xattr pass + source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update` (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, made public and layout-pinned; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct).
- `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` degrades a library-load failure to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` / `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in the pure core) instead of the raw FFI dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-lib fallback is impossible with native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader override) — documented in the RCA.

**Verification:**
- Repro tests now green: `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` (classification + clean-note through the engine and the `read` tool), `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` (installer layout contract, incl. static assertions on both shell installers) — 119 targeted tests pass.

# weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

Everything is committed to the branch and `outputs/response.md` is written. The task is complete:

**gh-1574 — SQLite reads failing on installed `fa` binaries: fixed.**

**Root cause** (verified empirically with a real `dart build cli` bundle): `package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart native assets — the AOT binary resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`, but every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary (`<install_dir>/lib`). For `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing; the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error.

**Fix (TDD — repro tests written first, confirmed failing):**
- Installers now write the libs where the binary looks (`<install_dir>/../lib`): `site/install.sh` (incl. the macOS quarantine-xattr pass + source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update` (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, made public and layout-pinned; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct).
- `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` degrades a library-load failure to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` / `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in the pure core) instead of the raw FFI dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-lib fallback is impossible with native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader override) — documented in the RCA.

**Verification:**
- Repro tests now green: `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` (classification + clean-note through the engine and the `read` tool), `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` (installer layout contract, incl. static assertions on both shell installers) — 119 targeted tests pass.
- Full CI-scope suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration,browser-ext`): **10,547 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures**.
- `dart analyze lib test bin`: no errors/warnings; `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` AC1–AC4 unchanged (one `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit — pre-existing, environment-specific).
- End-to-end proof: a relocated real native-assets binary with the new layout loads SQLite successfully.
